messages:
incident-bot: ALERT — reserved-capacity pool 'resv-prod-eu-01' at 100% GPU utilization, queue growth detected :rotating_light:

carla.sre: seeing sustained queue length on dispatcher (~1.2k requests), autoscaler returned 403 on scale request to provider. throttles started at 14:03 UTC

dave.k: I'm on-call. what's impacted? any customer-facing errors?

alice.eng: multiple enterprise tenants showing 429s and long tail latency (>20s). AcmeCorp reporting elevated error rates. Cloud metrics: GpuPoolUtilization = 100%, AutoscalerErrors = rate-limited (429 from provider API)

ben-accounts: pinging AcmeCorp account contact now. I'll draft a brief: outlining we are on it, likely impact, ETA for mitigation.

carla.sre: quick root cause snapshot: provider rate limit on instance creations. our fallback tries to provision new instances, provider denies. autoscaler backoff triggered; queue piles up. Noisy neighbor not confirmed yet but we have a tenant occupying many slots.

eve-ops: running: 
```
# list troubled reservations
redwoodctl pools describe resv-prod-eu-01 --format json | jq '.tenants | sort_by(.gpu_count) | reverse | .[0:10]'
```

alice.eng: top tenant is AcmeCorp-ml with 48 GPUs reserved and currently running heavy batch jobs. They are within their reservation but causing saturation for burst capacity.

dave.k: can we evict non-reserved workloads? any quick levers?

carla.sre: yes — we can temporarily pause bursts for best-effort customers and throttle batch jobs via rate-limit rules. Propose: 1) disable non-enterprise burst, 2) pause scheduled batch windows, 3) initiate eviction of low-priority pods.

alice.eng: adding a canary: route new requests for enterprise-tier to a compatible quantized model variant hosted in another region (higher latency but keeps customer flow). Will update routing policy.

incident-bot: Pager escalated to infra-sre (dave.k) @ 14:07 UTC. Incident severity: Sev2. Playbook: reserved-pool-exhaustion.

carla.sre: executing eviction command now:
```
redwoodctl evict --pool resv-prod-eu-01 --priority-best-effort --dry-run=false --max-evict 120
```

eve-ops: eviction in progress, freeing ~32 GPUs from best-effort tenants. Observability: queue shrank by ~300 in 90s.

eve-ops: provider reports 50% success on scaling requests after backoff window. Still seeing occasional 429s from provider quota.

dave.k: ben, update AcmeCorp: say we are mitigating and have a failover to a compatible region/quantized model; ETA 20m for stabilization. keep them informed.

ben-accounts: message sent to AcmeCorp legal+platform: "we're mitigating, expecting partial relief within 20-30m, no data loss, higher latency possible; will follow up." They replied ack.

carla.sre: follow-up mitigation: temporarily increase token-bucket for eviction throughput and enable priority preemption for jobs marked experimental. Also filed a provider support ticket for scale-rate increase.

alice.eng: routing switch done: enterprise calls now route to eu-s2 quantized variant with higher latency (~200ms extra) but success rate improves. Traffic shifted at 14:18 UTC.

eve-ops: metrics: 429s reduced by 78%, queue length now stable ~120. GPUs freed: 28. Autoscaler requests now within provider limits.

dave.k: handing off to morning oncall (carla.sre) at 14:34 UTC. Summary: provider rate limits blocked autoscaler, eviction freed GPUs, routing to quantized model reduced customer errors. Next: provider quota increase, tighten batch window controls, incident postmortem.

carla.sre: acknowledged handoff. I'll kick off postmortem doc and action items: 1) provider quota request, 2) add hard cap for best-effort during peak, 3) provide AcmeCorp post-incident report, 4) improve autoscaler exponential backoff jitter.

incident-bot: Incident update: mitigated -> monitoring. Time to mitigation: 18m. Incident channel will remain open for 2 hours for validation.

ben-accounts: AcmeCorp says they saw impact but grateful for quick mitigation. Asked for uplift on burst reservations for their nightly jobs — will coordinate next week.

dave.k: closing notes: assign owners for postmortem items and schedule a follow-up with provider. Great cross-team work :thumbsup:
